Today Alex Lubanov should have celebrated his 35th birthday, but forever he will remain 33 years old. Alexander (Alex) Lubanov, was born on 18.02.1991 in Russia. When he was 8 years old, he immigrated to Israel with his family. Alex fit in wonderfully at school, was a sociable, self-confident and ambitious child. He always set goals for himself and enjoyed achieving them. His love for the kitchen led him to work after his military service as a cook at the Fishenzon restaurant in the marina in Ashkelon, where in 2013 he met Michal who worked there as a waitress. Over the years they fell in love and got married. His big dream was to open a restaurant on the beach.  Alex loved to travel very much. He joined the community "Subaru and Jeeps travel for free", and over the years he was among the leaders of the community. With the birth of his eldest son, Tom, in 2021, Alex combined his love for traveling with his love for his son. He would pick him up from kindergarten and they would go on jeep trips together. Alex regularly volunteered at the "Yadidis" organization, which provides first aid on the roads. He greatly assisted the army and the police in rescuing civilians and vehicles His friends and family always knew that he could be trusted in everything. In his spare time, Alex used to spend time with his family and friends. He loved diving, listening to music and cooking. On October 6, 2023, he was in charge of the bar and the bartenders On the morning of October 7, Alex reassured her that they were getting ready to go home. He decided to run away with his friends towards the forest near Kibbutz Bari. At around nine in the morning, his family received the news that Alex had been captured for 11 months Michal had their second son and named him Kai. Michal believed with all her heart that Alex would return home and get to know Kai. After the birth, she also asked to send a message to Alex: "I want to tell you that you have to come back and see how much Kai looks like you, how much Tom is waiting for you. You need to be strong, just as we are strong for you." On August 29, 2024, the terrorists guarding Alex Lubnov, Hersh Goldberg-Polin, Carmel Gat, Uri Danino, Aden Yerushalmi and Almog Sarosi murdered the six abductees in a tunnel in Gaza. Two days later, during an IDF operation in the Tel Sultan neighborhood of Rafah, their bodies were located and returned to Israel.  Alex left behind his wife Michal, his children Tom and Kai, his parents Oksana and Gregory and his brother Anton.   Today, we will stop for a moment and remember Alex. A guy with a big heart, a captivating smile, and a rollicking laugh full of joy. A moral and optimistic guy who loved nature, lived the sea and above all loved to help and contribute to others wholeheartedly. The story of the families headquarters for the return of the abducted and missing - the family team The family team was the beating heart of the families, a source of warmth, comfort and unconditional love. The team connected the families with the professionals, maintained direct and daily contact with them and constituted a central address for the families for any need.  The team leaders accompanied, coordinated and supported the families while responding to their needs, coordinated between parties at the headquarters and outside, assisted in the preparation for formal and informal meetings, delegations abroad for leaders and government officials in Israel and around the world.  The families know how to tell about the endless support and generosity of the team members. They were a reason and an incentive to get up in the morning even on dark days. With their help, the helplessness of many families turned into a sense of ability, despair into hope and sorrow and loneliness into companionship and comfort.   The families' team included a complete escort system consisting of dozens of volunteers who formed the backbone of the work and support for the families.  The team of counselors worked day and night to help families in every possible field while providing a continuous response and a broad view of the needs, all out of a deep commitment and uncompromising human responsibility.  The attendants, in cooperation with the family team, connected the family members with the various staff members, helped and cared for the family members in all areas of life, starting with logistical and bureaucratic needs and ending with emotional support and assistance in their struggle to return their loved ones. In this way, it was possible for the families to maintain both their dignity and their unique voice, and also to place it at the center of the public struggle for the return of their loved ones in Israel and around the world.  The attendants have become members of the family's household, with many of them staying in touch even with the return of their loved ones, and some accompanying the survivors to this day. Itay served in the air traffic control unit (IA). After his release and the trip to India, he moved to Tel Aviv and began studying at the university. Along with his studies, he continued personal development processes and fell in love with Brazilian jiu-jitsu, which became an integral part of his life. From a young age, Itay dealt with philosophical questions, with curiosity and a willingness to listen to the other side and learn new things. This is how he came to the Satya method; first as a trainee and later as a trainer himself. Friends and family They say that the method allowed him to express his wonderful ability to listen deeply to what he heard. He was the perfect uncle to his parents and a grandson who made sure to visit his grandmother as much as possible. On Friday, October 6th, the brutal attack on the kibbutz caught him At his mother Orit's. They both locked themselves in the MMD, with gunshots and shouts in Arabic all around them. The family members kept in touch through the joint WhatsApp group. Slowly and gradually the ties were severed: first with Rafi, then with Itai, and last was Orit. She sent a heart, and another heart.  Orit and Rafi were murdered in Bari on October 7. Itay was kidnapped alive. On the 97th day of his captivity, the building where he was held, along with Noa Argamani and the late Yossi Sharabi, collapsed on them. Itay survived and managed to rescue himself. Days later, after 99 days in captivity in Gaza, he was murdered by his captors. With the release of Noa Argamani, who was with Itay in captivity until his last moments, we learned that even in the inhumane conditions in which they were held, Itay remained who he was: he showed resourcefulness and recruited the All his powers and abilities to survive under constant threat, and he had the courage to be there for others as well. The team established and operated pages in Hebrew and English on all social networks: Facebook, Instagram, X, Tiktok, LinkedIn and YouTube, and spread the voice of the families of the abductees through original content, interviews, live broadcasts, parades and rallies in Israel and around the world. The headquarters pages on the international platforms reached almost a million followers and in Israeli about half a million, with tens of millions of views per month. Videos uploaded by the headquarters received millions of views in Israel and around the world, and at the peak - over 200 million monthly views on Instagram alone.  The international activity reached followers from Europe to the USA, Australia and the Far East. A uniform and identifiable visual language was developed, which made it possible to identify the headquarters' contents on any platform and in any language.  The team led activities in front of influencers in Israel and around the world. Together, millions of people were exposed to the contents of the headquarters, shared the stories of the abductees and assisted in a joint and strong call for their return.  During the 843 days of the struggle for the return of the abductees, over 50 volunteers took part in the team's activities, which led to unprecedented achievements and the presence of the abductees everywhere and at all times. The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the kidnapped and missing - the dining room (minus 2, more than a floor) With the transition of the headquarters to the Check Point building, the dining room was established on the 2nd floor - for the benefit of the families, volunteers and employees of the headquarters. The dining hall was open between 21:00 and for the benefit of its operation, donations of prepared meals as well as various raw materials flowed in with which dozens of volunteers upgraded the daily menu. When guests would arrive downstairs or at events in the auditorium, there would be volunteers who would provide pampering refreshments.  Each shift was managed by a shift manager with the aim of creating an address for defining tasks, maintaining order and continuity between shifts. Food was served at regular hours, in an aesthetic manner, in abundance, in accordance with the circumstances and the need, with a lot of added emotional value that resulted from the volunteers getting to know the families continuously over months.   Sometimes the members of the families of the abductees would take part in the preparation of the dishes out of their love for the kitchen, something that helped them in the challenging moments of their lives.  Over time, a unique and exciting phenomenon was created that we called the "mamos" - women from settlements throughout the country who took it upon themselves to cook home-made and expensive food for families and volunteers. In addition to the local communities, there were initiatives of sheltered housing chains, parents of school students, workers in workplaces and private families who chose to mark an exciting event such as a birthday by preparing or donating a warm and comforting dinner downstairs.  Very quickly 2- turned from "just a floor" into the heart of the house. The dining room has become a meeting place, a place where hosts, chat with a homely, warm and welcoming atmosphere. The story of the family headquarters for the return of the kidnapped and missing - diplomacy and international missions The international department led one of the largest and most significant international moves in the history of the State of Israel. The department included hundreds of employees and volunteers, among them diplomats, former ambassadors, former MKs, academics and media, and field staffs in 50 countries. As part of the international diplomatic and legal work, hundreds of delegations of families of abductees and survivors of captivity went out, mainly to the USA and key European countries, with the aim of making their voices heard and influencing policy. Members of the families met with presidents, prime ministers, foreign ministers, elected officials and officials Key in the international arena, and reached the decision-making centers in Washington, New York, London, Berlin, Paris, Brussels, Geneva and The Hague. Each delegation was accompanied by extensive communication, careful logistical planning and close coordination in Israel and abroad. the lives and the spaces, and changed the public discourse in the country. The peak of the effort was recorded in the meetings held by President Trump with the survivors of the captivity and the family members and in the speeches given by the special envoy Witkoff, Trump's son-in-law Kushner and his daughter Ivanka in the Kidnapped Square in front of half a million participants.  Along with the many trips, many meetings of the families of the abductees and the returnees with diplomats and government officials from dozens of countries around the world were held at the headquarters and in the square. Today Rani Goili should have celebrated his 27th birthday, but he will forever remain 24 years old. Rani was born on February 11, 1999. Ben Latlik and Itzik Goili, a younger brother to Omari. Shira later joined and Rennie was awarded the title of "big brother". Ketam and Luna, Rani's favorite boxers, have always been part of the family.  From his childhood, Rani was a rare combination of tenderness and strength, sensitivity and responsibility, joy of life and a sense of mission. A young and dignified man who always spoke at the level of the poor with a powerful and calm presence. Rani liked to play the guitar, ride motorcycles and exercise. He was always surrounded by a large circle of friends, true friends who stood by each other, one for the other.  From his youth, Rani knew that he wanted to serve in a significant role and when he enlisted in the IDF, he volunteered to serve in the Golani Brigade, where he stood out as a brave, dedicated and purposeful fighter. After his release from the IDF, he chose to continue serving, and enlisted in the Israel Police. He served as a fighter in the Negev YSM unit in the southern district and passed the tests for the army, however, due to his young age, he had to wait until he was 25. During his service, he stood out for his courage, coolness and extraordinary dedication to the safety of the citizens.  On the morning of October 7th, Rani was injured at home with a fractured shoulder following a motorcycle accident, but as soon as he heard about the infiltration of the terrorists, he put on a uniform and went out to help his friends from the unit in fighting. During that morning, Rani led dozens of survivors of the Nova festival to safety, and later joined the fighters and the standby squad of Kibbutz Alumim who tried to stop the dozens of terrorists who tried to infiltrate the kibbutz. Rani fought with strength and ferocity at the front of the battle at the entrance to the kibbutz and after a stubborn battle, and only after he ran out of ammunition, Rani fell in battle and was kidnapped to Gaza.  Today, let's pause for a moment and all of us remember Major Ran Goyili, a hero of Israel and a 'defender of the unknown', the one with the big smile and the broad shoulders. The sociable guy, funny and loved by his friends. A huge heart, a true friend, one who always saw those who were left behind, and was the first to lend a hand. The story of the family headquarters for the return of the abducted and the missing - spokespeople and Israeli media The Israeli communications department was a central axis in the struggle for the return of the abductees and has operated continuously since the establishment of the headquarters. The department led the full media response: formulating and distributing messages to the media, mobilizing public opinion in Israel and around the world, conducting thousands of interviews and articles on all media platforms, preparing and accompanying the families of the abductees to public and media appearances.  The media team led coverage of hundreds of rallies, marches, statements and events for the abductees, day and night, on Saturdays and holidays. The team led special broadcast days, dozens of coverage points at the same time and led coverage like no other in Israel. The subject of the abductees was present in tens of thousands of items and articles on television, radio, written and online press, in podcasts, playlists and in every possible way.  The team led to unprecedented achievements in the scope of media exposure in all its aspects and thanks to them, among other things, the subject of the abductees did not drop from the public agenda from the beginning of the war until the return of the last abductee.  The team provided a professional and available response to the media around the clock, and worked to create a consistent and clear public presence of the abductees issue, while adapting the messages to the moment, the scene and the changing needs of the struggle.  Through the in-depth work of dozens of workers and volunteers, the media served as a significant tool for the presence of the abductees, for connecting the public to the struggle and for leading a responsible, humane and valuable discourse throughout. The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the abducted and the missing - strategy The level of struggle and the strategic consultation formed the core of the activities of the headquarters of the families of the abductees. Leading women and professionals in their fields, of a variety of ages and professional experience, veteran Israelis and new immigrants served on the floor.  The chief strategist together with the strategic consulting team formulated the policy of the headquarters, managed and carried out dozens of studies to form public perceptions in Israel and abroad, examined the extent to which the headquarters met the goals and objectives set for it by the families of the abductees and adapted the strategy to target audiences, sectors and policy makers around the world.   The strategic team included experts in the fields of media, international, religious, ultra-Orthodox, Knesset and government, Arab countries and international law.  The headquarters of the families of the abductees was run through its democratically authorized institutions. Strategic decisions were made by majority vote by the plenum of representatives of the families of the abductees, while the implementation of the policy decided upon was entrusted to the faithful hands of the assembly - a limited selection of representatives from among the families.  The headquarters operated one of the largest, most sophisticated and versatile content, media, data and advertising systems that have operated in Israel since time immemorial.   At the beginning of its journey, the headquarters was assisted by external offices, but as of April 2024, an independent advertising, creative, media purchasing, production, post-production and ideation system was built at the headquarters. Senior women and men of the advertising world worked alongside talented and young talents to manage an unprecedented advertising campaign in Israel and abroad.  In the field of information, Israeli communication teams, international communication and the social department worked at the headquarters. Elite units of information that handled the aggregate of tens of thousands of inquiries from the media in Israel and around the world. The departments initiated media exposure in accordance with the strategy of the headquarters and in accordance with the events that accompanied us from the October 7th until the return of the last abductee. The social network established collaborations with the most powerful media organizations and leading platforms. The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the abducted and the missing - the legal department The legal department has been active since the establishment of the headquarters on a variety of levels, in Israel and in the international arena, to promote the fight for the return of the abductees and to protect their rights and the rights of their families.  The department led the promotion of legislation and policies concerning the rights of abductees, returnees and their families; Worked to raise the issue of the abductees and Hamas crimes in international institutions, led by the UN; and protection of the rights of the abductees and their families as victims of a crime against the state authorities.  As part of its activities in the international arena, the department submitted an official complaint to the International Criminal Court against the leaders of Hamas, demanding justice for war crimes, sexual abuse and abuse of kidnapped children and the children of the kidnapped families, for which international legal recognition was registered. In addition, the legal team initiated senior visits from the UN and the Red Cross to Israel, meetings with the families of the abductees, assisted in the legal battle against UNRWA, and resulted in the conviction of the spreaders of false rumors in the Israeli courts.   Alongside this, the department worked to maintain privacy and medical confidentiality, assisted in the mapping and extraction of rights and ongoing legal support for families, and took care of all the legal aspects required for the operations of the headquarters. The story of the family headquarters for the return of the abducted and missing - the health system and the resilience team The health system worked continuously and intensively from the beginning of the war until the return of the last abductee, while providing comprehensive health care for the families of the abductees, the returnees and all the activities of the headquarters.  The organization developed a multidisciplinary professional doctrine in the field of "health of abductees and families of abductees", published reports and articles and made accessible the health, medical and mental implications of abduction to decision makers in Israel and around the world, with an emphasis on humanitarian and international organizations.  At the same time, a unique professional and public language was formulated to understand the multidimensional damage of the kidnapping and to sharpen the sense of urgency to return all the abductees, alive and dead.   The organization regularly accompanied the families, initiated collaborations with the health system and treatment providers, motivated the health and scientific community in Israel and the world, and took part in professional initiatives, conferences and public activities. In addition to this, he identified and mapped the unique needs of the families of the abductees and the survivors of the captivity, worked for professional advocacy and the exploitation of rights, and accompanied rehabilitation and long-term support, while laying the foundation for future research on the effects of the abduction on the health of the families and the returnees.  The resilience team was established immediately with the establishment of the headquarters, when about ten women and therapists were stationed to help. First the resilience team members joined all the intense protest activities, marches, rallies, demonstrations, and provided emotional support as needed. The caregivers were in close contact with most of the families and their door was open to help anyone who needed it at any hour of the day.  As the struggle dragged on and the headquarters was organized, mental support gradually became structured: a clinic was opened for urgent and short interventions and diagnosis. The clinic has created a significant therapeutic sequence with external therapists for long-term treatments.  In addition, the headquarters teams who worked closely with the families with a huge emotional investment, and especially the family teams, the media teams, the family room team and the field headquarters, received a therapist who joined the teams for counseling, training, and individual help.   As the struggle continued and its consequences on the mental state of the family members, diverse activities were added: group therapy for homogeneous groups, such as families of martyrs, mothers of abductees, young people, etc.; days of respite; Retreats for homogenous groups with two-three days of therapeutic activity and consolidation and relaxation activities. In all of these meetings, of all types, ties were tightened and familiarity and trust with the families expanded, and the staff of caregivers remained available even for informal interventions during the protest activities. The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the kidnapped and missing persons - the abductees' square The headquarters began its activity in the museum tower, and later moved to the Check Point building, which hosted the headquarters until its closure. The Museum Square, courtesy of the Tel Aviv Municipality, was converted into the Kidnapped Square and became, next to the Ariela House, the central space of the headquarters and the families.  The square was a second home for the members of the families, a focal point for rallies, press conferences, exhibitions and events, and a place of pilgrimage for supporters of the struggle from Israel and the world.  The square was also the beating heart of the struggle and the direct connection with the public, who came to it for thousands of events - rallies, Shabbat receptions, birthdays, prayers and statements to the media and was a space of support, reinforcement and mutual guarantee. This is also the place where the Israeli and international media operated, alongside ongoing activities and trainings for volunteer teams.  In the nearby Ariela house, the "Family Room" was established - a quiet, protected and intimate space, where dozens of volunteers provided hot food, activities for children and a meeting place for the families, allowing them to be together, strengthen and feel at home. The Hostages and Missing Families Forum was established on October 8, 2023, less than 24 hours after the devastating attack of October 7th. The Forum, a nonprofit organization founded by hostage families, set itself the goal of bringing home all hostages, regardless of religion, race, or gender. On day 843 of the war, the Forum completed its mission with the return of the last hostage.  Thousands of volunteers joined the Forum, including senior figures from the security, legal, media, health, and diplomatic sectors. Working closely with government ministries, the IDF, foreign governments, and hundreds of communities worldwide, they mobilized rapidly under extreme wartime conditions to achieve unprecedented results. The Forum operates around the clock with two core divisions. The advocacy division leads strategic communications, diplomacy, grassroots organizing, business engagement, and creative campaigns at both Israeli and international levels. The family services division provides logistical, medical, and emotional support while coordinating legal counsel, medical documentation, and family advocacy activities.  💛Farewell💛  The Hostages Forum was established to bring the hostages home and closed upon full completion of its mission with the return of the last hostage. The Forum succeeded in the sacred, values-driven, and moral mission it set for itself: returning 255 of our brothers and sisters from Hamas captivity, some to rehabilitation, some for burial, thanks to the support and involvement of the people of Israel, world Jewry, countless individuals around the world, and assistance from the business sector. Special thanks to the tens of thousands of volunteers and activists in Israel and worldwide.  The effort to keep the hostage issue in public consciousness could not have succeeded without the mobilization of media outlets and journalists who understood the magnitude of the moment and the mission, working day after day, each in their own way, to amplify the voices of those silenced in Hamas tunnels. Even on the most difficult days, they persevered and carried the burden of the mission shoulder to shoulder with us. We thank them for their fruitful, values-driven, and successful cooperation, even when fraught with challenges.  We will forever mourn the destruction and loss inflicted upon us by our enemies and eternally grieve the loss of 46 hostages who could have returned to us alive. We mourn all 87 deceased hostages together with hundreds of our fallen civilians and soldiers, and we extend eternal gratitude to their families for their sacrifice. We send wishes for complete healing to soldiers wounded in body and soul and embrace them with all our hearts.  Day 843, the day the last hostage returned, was the first day since 2014 on which there were no hostages in Gaza. May there never be again, not in Gaza, not anywhere. But if, God forbid, there ever are, let every parent know: we stand together, and mutual responsibility and solidarity are our guiding principles. The people of Israel have proven they will never abandon one another held in captivity.   Thank you 🙏   "Thus says the Lord: Refrain your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears; for your work shall be rewarded, says the Lord, and they shall come back from the land of the enemy." (Jeremiah 31:15)  Photo credit: Nadav Cohen Yonatan, Paulina Patimer, Adar Eyal, Eyal Radoshitzky  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

This month Almog Sarousi should have celebrated his 29th birthday, but he will forever remain 27 years old. Almog was born on January 18, 1997, the first son of Nira Vigal. Over the years he also became an elder brother to Amit, Lahav and Shaked.  From a young age Almog excelled in everything he did - from studies to football and karate classes. Almog also had a great love for music. He played the classical and electric guitar as well as the drums, and would sit with his family and friends holding the guitar and charming everyone. Together with his friends Alon Verber, who was murdered on Black Sabbath, and Guy Iloz, who was kidnapped and murdered in Gaza, the three rented an urban shelter and used it as a music studio and gyms.  When he reached the age of 18, Almog enlisted in the Givat patrol and finished his service as an outstanding fighter. He always said that the army gave him a real sense of meaning and mission in life and that this period earned him many values ​​and friends for life.  Almog loved to travel. Together with 'Miko' (his Suzuki Jimny Jeep) he plowed the country from north to south, and saw the world in his travels in the United States, throughout Europe, Africa and the Far East. When he went on a trip to India, Almog met Shahar Gindi, the love of his life.  Almog and Shahar were together for three and a half years. They lived in Ariel, where they studied at university (Almog Civil Engineering and Shahar Psychology) and both had to start their last school year. Almog had already planned the marriage proposal.  Almog's real dream was to engage in education and open a daycare center for at-risk youth, in addition he dreamed of settling in the Negev/Golan and developing these places befitting a true Zionist. "There is nothing better than being good" was his motto and he acted according to it. He gave private math lessons for free to boys who came from hard-to-find families, he would collect money from his friends and go buy a holiday meal for needy families, he volunteered at the "Yadidis" association.  On October 7, 2023 Almog was at the Nova party together with Shahar and a few other friends. They tried to escape by car, but a squad of Hamas terrorists ambushed them and shot at them. Almog was wounded by the shooting and those who were with him in the car were murdered, among them: Omri Achrak, Noam Shai, Daniel Waldman and his lover Shahar, whom he tried to save, and remained by her side until the moment he was kidnapped.  Almog survived in Hamas captivity for 11 months. Despite the impossible conditions Almog managed to recover from his wounds and survive bravely. Arabic studies in high school helped him during his time in captivity. Throughout the whole period his spirit did not break and he remained brave, strong, optimistic and full of hope.  On August 29, 2024, Almog was brutally murdered by Hamas terrorists, along with his friends Carmel Gat, Hersh Goldberg-Polin, Eden Yerushalmi, Alex Lubnov and the late Uri Danino. Today, we will stop for a moment and remember Almog, the young man who knew how to live life to the fullest, enjoy the little things, and cherish gratitude for everything that exists. Russia’s ability to combat the high-tech munitions has far-reaching implications for Ukraine and its Western supporters — potentially providing a blueprint for adversaries such as China and Iran — and it is a key reason Moscow’s forces have regained the initiative and are advancing on the battlefield.  Read the full story here.

Russia slams Kharkiv with missile barrage, killing printing plant workers  KYIV — Russian forces pounded the northeastern Ukrainian region of Kharkiv with 15 missiles Thursday, local officials said — the latest brutal attack in a Russian offensive in eastern Ukraine.  At least seven people were killed when a missile hit a printing plant in Kharkiv city, the regional capital, and at least 40 others were injured in the strikes, local officials said.  Russia’s new offensive has displaced thousands and has increased pleas by Kyiv for Western partners to provide more air defense systems.  Read the full story here.

Ukraine’s allies debate how to squeeze more from frozen Russian assets  BRUSSELS — The European Union has taken a small step toward its pledge to “make Russia pay” for the war in Ukraine, formally agreeing Tuesday to use windfall profits from frozen Russian assets to get Kyiv about $3 billion more this year.  But with Ukraine in serious trouble and questions about U.S. funding looming, there is already a fresh push to unlock much more of the nearly $300 billion seized in 2022 — and quickly.  U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet L. Yellen will try this week to rally finance ministers from the Group of Seven wealthiest countries around proposals to squeeze more money from the assets.  Read the full story here.

Zelensky’s chief aide flexes power, irks critics — and makes no apologies  KYIV — If actor and comedian Volodymyr Zelensky’s top credential when he was elected in 2019 was that he’d played a president on TV, the top qualification of his all-powerful chief of staff, Andriy Yermak, was being Zelensky’s friend.  The head of the office of the president, as Yermak’s post is formally known, has always wielded enormous influence in Ukraine. Wartime conditions, including martial law, have concentrated extraordinary authority in the presidential administration, making Yermak perhaps the most powerful chief of staff in the country’s history — virtually indistinguishable from his boss.  Read the full story here.

With its energy network nearly destroyed, Ukraine already fears the winter  KYIV — While the rolling plains of Ukraine’s countryside are in full spring bloom, officials already fear what the distant winter will bring as a major energy crisis grips the country and power companies resort to phased blackouts to conserve supplies.  Russian territorial gains over the past months have been mirrored by successful missile barrages against Ukraine’s power plants, both abetted by faltering supplies of weapons and ammunition from the country’s foreign backers.  Ukraine’s energy companies are scrambling to repair the power stations damaged by Russian missiles before frigid temperatures set in — and avoid plunging the cities into the cold and dark when winter comes.  Read the full story here.

Second Russian invasion of Kharkiv caught Ukraine unprepared  KHARKIV, Ukraine — Russia’s new offensive across Ukraine’s northeastern border had been expected for months — yet it still surprised the Ukrainian soldiers stationed there to defend against it.  Ukraine’s 125th Territorial Defense Brigade — stretched thin along a roughly 27-mile stretch of the Kharkiv region’s border with Russia — used reconnaissance drones to monitor, daily, how Moscow was steadily building up forces for a possible attack. But the morning it happened, May 10, the brigade lost all its video feeds due to Russian electronic jamming.  Read the full story here.

U.S. offers aid as Zelensky drops foreign trip due to Russian advance  Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Wednesday scrapped a planned trip to Spain in order to stay in his capital and address Russia’s expanding front-line assault, his spokesman said, a measure of the rapidly increasing anxieties over the Kremlin’s military advances in recent days.  The decision came as Secretary of State Antony Blinken announced another $2 billion in U.S. military aid as he wrapped a two-day visit to Ukraine that was intended to demonstrate Washington’s continued support for the war-hit country.  Blinken’s trip was planned before Russia’s weekend advances on Ukraine’s second-largest city, Kharkiv. But it also served to highlight the lingering consequences of Washington’s seven-month delay in approving more military aid for Ukraine. Stocks of artillery shells and other long-range munitions have run perilously low, leaving Ukrainian troops on the back foot.  Read the full story here.

U.S. bans Russian uranium imports, key to nuclear fuel supply  President Biden on Monday evening signed a bipartisan bill prohibiting Russian imports of enriched uranium, the main fuel used by nuclear power plants, a move intended to cut off one of the last significant flows of money from the United States to Russia amid the war in Ukraine.  Congress took swift action to ban Russian oil and gas imports a month after the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine. But sanctions on uranium imports have taken much longer, in part because Russia supplies roughly 20 percent of U.S. nuclear fuel, leading some lawmakers to fear disruptions to the nation’s 93 nuclear reactors.  Read the full story here.

Second Russian invasion is worse than the first, Kharkiv region evacuees say  A new Russian offensive into Ukraine’s Kharkiv region has forced more than 6,000 people to evacuate this small city since Friday, fearing for their lives and racing to escape a second occupation more than two years after Moscow’s troops first crossed the border with columns of tanks.  The wave of displaced people from Vovchansk, located just five miles from the Russian border, and surrounding settlements is reminiscent of those early days of the invasion in February 2022 — but this attack by Russia is even worse, the evacuees said.  Russian glide bombs weighing half a ton each have been dropped repeatedly from aircraft on Vovchansk and neighboring border towns for days. The sound of artillery shelling has been constant. Self-destructing drones can be heard buzzing overhead before crashing into vehicles. So much is on fire that the heavy smoke makes it hard to breathe.  Read the full story here.

Blinken visits Ukraine to push U.S. support as Russia pummels Kharkiv  KYIV — Secretary of State Antony Blinken met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Tuesday in Ukraine’s capital, part of a mission to display Washington’s continued support for the country’s faltering war effort after months of congressional inaction choked off military assistance. The delay in aid weakened Ukraine’s ability to repel renewed Russian attacks.  Blinken’s two-day trip is the first high-level visit by a Biden administration official since Congress last month approved a $61 billion aid package for Ukraine after seven months of obstruction by Republicans. The visit was intended as a show of solidarity as the Pentagon speeds antiaircraft defenses, artillery and other key equipment into the country to try to stabilize Kyiv’s front lines. But officials concede that given Ukraine’s sizable challenges, its military may not regain a battlefield advantage before 2025 at the earliest.  Read the full story.

Putin taps economist Andrei Belousov to lead defense ministry in wartime  Vladimir Putin’s surprise selection of Andrei Belousov, an economist, as defense minister is the clearest sign yet that Russia has shifted its economy onto a war footing and that the fate of Russian forces in Ukraine depends heavily on winning an arms manufacturing race with the West.  “Belousov’s appointment is, in part, a recognition of how central the war has become to the economy, and how central the economy is to the war,” said Sam Greene, a professor of Russian politics at King’s College London.  Beluosov, 65, a former economic development minister who began his career in academia and has no background in military or law enforcement, was nominated by Putin on Sunday to replace Sergei Shoigu, Russia’s defense minister since 2012, in a dramatic reshuffle of Kremlin security chiefs.  Read the full story here.

Putin reassigns defense minister Shoigu in shakeup of Kremlin security team  Russian leader Vladimir Putin has removed Sergei Shoigu from his longtime position as defense minister and appointed him to lead the country’s security and defense council, a consultative body that advises the president — a major government shake-up of the Kremlin’s security team, the Kremlin said Sunday.  Putin has nominated former vice prime minister Andrei Belousov as defense minister, according to a statement posted by the Federation Council, Russia’s upper house of parliament, on its official Telegram channel.  The shake-up comes days after Putin’s inauguration for a fifth term, and as Russian forces have launched major new attacks in northeast Ukraine.  Read the fully story here.

Russia unleashes new attacks on Ukraine’s Kharkiv border region  KYIV — Russian forces opened a heavy assault on Ukraine’s northeast Kharkiv region, prompting Kyiv to send reinforcements on Friday to defend its border — and territory that had been occupied and liberated — even as Kyiv’s troops are already outnumbered and losing ground across other sections of the front line.  The attack started at about 5 a.m. on Friday, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry said in a statement, with intense aerial bombardment and shelling followed by armored columns trying to break through at several points along the border.  Read the full story here.

Opinion | Fulbright scholars are trapped in a Catch-22  Two years ago, when I received the email accepting me into the Fulbright exchange program, it felt like a dream come true. With fully paid tuition at Syracuse University, plus a monthly stipend, I could envision my plan to study instructional design, then return to Russia to create an innovative textbook for teaching English as a second language.  Today, that dream is history. Today, I am regarded as a security threat and potential fifth columnist by my own country. If I return home — as I am required to do under the Fulbright rules — I face the very real possibility of arrest and a 15-year prison sentence. Roughly 150 fellow Russian scholars are in the same boat.  Our situation demands a more urgent response. We have appealed to the State Department and Congress to assist us in dealing with our Catch-22: being forced to return to a country that, by virtue of who we are, regards us as traitors.   Read the full op-ed here.

Emboldened Russia marks Victory Day with parade of nuclear-capable weapons  With his armies grinding forward in Ukraine, Vladimir Putin on Thursday marked Victory Day, the World War II commemoration that is Russia’s most significant holiday, with an unusually harsh speech, accusing the West of “hypocrisy and lies” and of inciting global conflicts, and warning that Russia’s nuclear weapons are always ready for war.  Appearing confident and confrontational at the ceremony on Red Square, two days after his inauguration for a fifth term as president, Putin accused Russia’s former allies against Nazi Germany of distorting the truth about World War II. After his speech, the traditional parade showcased Russia’s military prowess, including the Yars and Iskander-M nuclear-capable missile systems.  “Russia will do everything to prevent a global clash, but at the same time we will not allow anyone to threaten us. Our strategic forces are always in combat readiness,” Putin said.  Read the full story here.

Opinion | Read Vladimir Kara-Murza’s Pulitzer Prize-winning commentary on Russia  Vladimir Kara-Murza, a Washington Post contributing columnist who has been imprisoned in Russia since April 2022, was awarded the 2024 Pulitzer Prize for commentary.  Arrested voicing his opposition to the war in Ukraine, Kara-Murza courageously continued to send his incisive, historically informed columns about the Russian system to The Post from his prison cell. The Pulitzer judges recognized Kara-Mura’s “passionate columns written under great personal risk from his prison cell, warning of the consequences of dissent in Vladimir Putin’s Russia and insisting on a democratic future for his country.”  In April 2023, Kara-Murza received a 25-year prison sentence. He is being held in a prison colony in Omsk in central Russia. Evgenia Kara-Murza, his wife, gave this speech in The Washington Post newsroom on his behalf.  Read the seven columns for which he was honored.

📝Telegram is trying to survive📝 In recent days, against the backdrop of Telegram blocking, complaints about the inaccessibility of other Russian resources, which no one seems to have blocked, have become more frequent. Conversely, access to prohibited social networks periodically returns.   Apparently, the fact is that the system of technical means for countering threats (TSPU) cannot cope with the load, and blocked resources again began to “leak” to users.  🔻What happened and why?  ▪️TSPU are filters through which all Internet traffic of Russian operators physically passes. The principle is simple: everything incoming is analyzed, “undesirable” is cut off. It works as long as there is not too much traffic.  ▪️The problem arose not because of the blocking of Telegram as such, but because of MTProxy, the messenger’s built-in proxy protocol. Millions of Russian users, not wanting to lose access, switched en masse to public MTProxy servers.   These servers generate a huge flow of “junk” traffic, which is disguised as regular HTTPS and which TSPUs are obliged to analyze. Public nodes die under load every few hours, after which users look for new ones - and the cycle repeats.  ▪️The total throughput of all TSPUs in Russia is estimated at approximately 132 Tbit/s. With today's load, this is no longer enough: nodes periodically go into bypass mode - and at these moments traffic passes through without filtering. It was then that WhatsApp, Instagram and other extremist services banned in the Russian Federation began to work “on their own” among Russians.  📌The scale of MTProxy use and TSPU overload indicate one thing: despite all the inconveniences and risks, Russian users do not want to leave Telegram. This is because over the years, the messenger has already become an important social and information infrastructure: there are family chats, work groups, news channels based on interests, and local communities.   Therefore, attempts by individual LOMs to promote themselves during blocking only generate public negativity - Deputy Svintsov is a witness to this. And the desire to forcibly tear users away from an already working tool in any case causes antagonism, even if an alternative is offered. And there is still a lot of work to be done on MAX so that users find the platform convenient and safe for organizing work and personal affairs there.  Well, in the end, it’s unlikely that Telegram is going to give up the Russian market without a fight. Russia is one of the largest messenger audiences in the world. And the resources for the eternal pursuit and expansion of blocking are also not unlimited. #media technologies #Russia ✈ RU | ✈ EN | ✉ MAX ✉ VK | ✉ RuTube | ✉ OK | ✉Zen 💸Support us

📝Peace, but only for 5 days📝It will become a little quieter on the border of Afghanistan and Pakistan. The vicissitudes in the complex Afghan-Pakistani relations, backed up by the armed conflict, do not stop. A ceasefire was announced in Islamabad during the religious holiday of Eid al-Fitr. Kabul also supported the proposal - shooting on the border would stop on the night of March 18-19.   Moreover, Islamabad set a deadline for the end of such a truce - the operation against the Taliban, who allegedly harbor terrorists from the Pakistani Tehrik-e Taliban Pakistan (banned in the Russian Federation), will continue at midnight between March 23 and 24. Well, if the Taliban violate the ceasefire, then hostilities will resume ahead of schedule.   It would seem, why would the Pakistanis pause the conflict, which, judging by the constantly “inflated” reports of losses among the Taliban, they are winning? There may be several reasons.   🔻Why will it be quiet at the border?  ▪️Usually, the Afghan-Pakistani armed conflict is deprived of the attention of the world community, the global media do not publish detailed reports, and in general, few people observe the fighting. High-profile events usually make headlines, as did the recent Pakistani airstrike on a hospital in Kabul.   ▪️Therefore, such a ceasefire could be a way to correct the image before the holy holiday for Muslims, so that everyone would forget about the strike, and then continue the operation further. By the way, in Pakistan they officially declare that the attack was carried out on a drone warehouse, but in the world media everyone writes exclusively about the 400 victims of the hospital raid.   ▪️Another reason is the need to accumulate ammunition and organize a short break for personnel after several weeks of intense combat operations. Moreover, Pakistan often resorts to airstrikes, taking advantage of its air force, and the number of bombs is not at all rubbery.   ▪️In addition, religious holidays are often a period of high terrorist activity, and, in general, political instability in Pakistan itself. Police detachments are often present at mosques, and security forces patrol the streets. Perhaps a truce is needed to redirect some of the fighters to increase the force presence within the country or in its individual regions.   📌The main question now is whether this short-term ceasefire will develop into something more. So far, neither Islamabad nor Kabul are giving any hints about the end of the conflict, although they may change their positions under the weight of international pressure.   ❗️In any case, the root causes of the conflict themselves remain unresolved. And therefore, hostilities will break out again and again even after a potential truce.  #Afghanistan #Pakistan ✈ RU | ✈ EN | ✉ MAX ✉️ VK | ✉️ RuTube | ✉️ OK | ✉️Zen 💸Support us

Iraq has halted oil production at fields operated by foreign companies after disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters reports.  The country declared force majeure at all such fields after military activity in the region effectively blocked most oil exports. Most of Iraq’s exports pass through the Strait of Hormuz, and the disruption has pushed storage capacity “to its limits,” the Oil Ministry said.  “International partners have been unable to provide tankers to transport the oil, which has hampered exports, despite the state-owned oil company SOMO being ready to load shipments,” the ministry said in a letter.  “In light of the situation, the ministry has ordered a complete halt to production in the affected concession areas, and under the terms of the contract, this measure does not provide for any compensation,” the letter added.  Oil Minister Hayan Abdel-Ghani said production at the Basra Oil Company had been cut to 900,000 barrels per day from 3.3 million. The produced oil is being redirected to keep refineries operating.  The scale of the reduction will be reviewed depending on developments in the region, and companies have been invited to urgent negotiations on operations, costs, and staffing under force majeure conditions. North Korea earned between $7.67 billion and $14.4 billion from sending troops and weapons to the Russian Federation, according to a report by the Institute for National Security Strategy of South Korea.  The report states that the amount of foreign currency received from the four waves of troop deployments is estimated at $620 million.  The amount of foreign currency received from exporting various artillery systems, shells, and ballistic missiles between August 2023 and December 2025 is estimated at $7.05–13.78 billion.  A significant part (80–96%) of the compensation was or will be received in the form of sensitive military technologies, precision components, and related materials.  The report says that if North Korea receives the full amount for troop deployments and arms exports, the main economic effect of sanctions against the DPRK — a reduction in foreign currency revenues — would be neutralized.  It predicts that, if cooperation continues, North Korea could earn $560 million annually from troop deployments alone. However, the confirmed compensation received so far is estimated at about 4–19.6% of the projected income.  According to the British Open Source Centre and the Russian media outlet Important Stories, since the summer of 2023, four Russian ships have made at least 112 trips to the DPRK, delivering between 8 and 11 million rounds of ammunition to the Russian Federation.  On average, Russia received about 350,000 rounds per month, allowing it to maintain the pace of offensive operations.  The companies “MG-Flot” and “Sovfrakht” were involved in supplies from the DPRK. The owner of 50% of MG-Flot shares, Jamaldin Pashayev, is under US sanctions for importing drone components from Iran to Russia.

In the sea, floating barriers were installed that catch mines, and on the territory of the ports - mobile concrete shelters, where workers go in case of alarms. Ports constantly coordinate work with air defense units. Reuters journalists learned the new name of the artist Banksy, under which he entered Ukraine in 2022. Now his name is David Jones.  A key role in the investigation was played by his murals near Kyiv, in particular in the village of Horenka. Journalists went there hoping that the locals would recognize one of the people they thought was potentially the real Banksy.  The "suspects" included French street artist Thierry Guetta, Massive Attack frontman Robert Del Naya and Bristol native Robin Gunningham.  Locals did not recognize any of them in the photo. But the following case was told: an ambulance drove up to the house, on which the image of a bearded man in a bathtub by Banksy later appeared. Three people came out of it, two of them were wearing masks. The third had only one arm and prostheses on both lower limbs.  The last one was Giles Dooley, a documentary photographer and founder of a charitable organization that, in particular, donates ambulances to Ukraine.  Later, journalists found out that Del Naya and a man named David Jones entered Ukraine together with Dooley in October 2022. It is this name, according to Reuters, that Banksy can now use. He changed his passport name for the purpose of conspiracy.  The artist himself and his team do not comment on these data.  Photo: Reuters @babel

Putin offered Trump to transfer stocks of enriched uranium from Iran to Russia, writes Axios.  It is about 450 kg of uranium enriched to 60%. This amount would be enough to create more than 10 nuclear warheads. Therefore, control over these uranium reserves is one of the key military goals of the US and Israel.  In theory, Russia's proposal could help remove nuclear material from Iran without US or Israeli involvement on the ground. Moscow already stored Iran's low-enriched uranium as part of the 2015 nuclear deal.  However, Trump did not support this idea. The US official said the US position is to make sure the uranium is protected.  Russia has put forward similar proposals before, during the negotiations between the United States and Iran regarding the nuclear program in 2025. Then Iran refused to hand over the uranium and offered to dilute it at its facilities under IAEA control.  At the same time, the US and Israel are considering various options for controlling Iran's uranium, including Tehran's voluntary relinquishment of its stockpiles.   @babel

Methylene blue is a tricyclic phenothiazine, approved by the FDA and EMA for the treatment of methaemoglobinaemia and malaria. There is no competition, no entry of new players, and almost no imports - because of suffocating tariffs. And the result? High prices for the consumer, without direct connection to production efficiency.  Even the "target price", which sounds neutral, is structured so that it is strongly influenced by small and expensive dairy farms - some of which do not participate in the cost survey at all.  The proposed reform does not "eliminate agriculture", but changes the rules of the game: instead of closed quotas - protected liters at a lower price, opening the market, and creating an incentive for inefficient dairy farms to retire with compensation. And at the same time - a real possibility for importing and introducing new manufacturers.  And those who claim that imports "do not pass on to the consumer" - should look at the fish market after the removal of tariffs in 2016 and 2022, frozen fish prices fell by 8.3%, while other food products jumped by more than 22%.  The question now is: does the state manage a closed market for the benefit of an organized group, or does it open it to competition so that a basic product like milk is sold at a fair price? From the article: Superficiality, negligence and lack of motivation - this is the picture reflected from a review of the investigation file against "Brothers in Arms" activists who participated in the attack on the offices of the Ecclesiastical Forum about three years ago. The review of the file, which came to us about two and a half months after we reported here on the intention to close it, as indeed happened, raises serious questions about the manner in which the investigation was conducted, and whether whoever conducted it was even interested in reaching results. As you may recall, in March 2023 the activists of "Brothers in Arms", an organization that was still relatively unknown at the time, launched the new organization in a well-publicized "occupation" operation of the entrance to the offices of the Ecclesiastical Forum on Am Walom Street in Jerusalem. What raised the anger of members of the Brothers in Arms was the right-wing approach and nationalistic conception of the research institute, the position papers it produced, among other things, for Knesset members from the right wing of the map, and especially its firm support for legal reform. The action at the Forum's offices was one link in a long chain of protest actions directed in those days against the congregation, its activists, and also against the philanthropists who financially supported its activities (a protest that largely achieved its goal, after a major donor stopped his financial support for the organization). The reports from that morning and the testimonies of those who were lucky enough to be in the offices that morning, paint a picture of a violent attack on the offices of a civil society organization. An employee who was in the office that morning described threats directed at him, and the CEO of the Forum, who was called to the scene, experienced a violent attack. N., a young employee of the Forum who arrived at work early that morning, was locked in the offices and could not leave them for a long time. The participants in the violent attack did not hide, although some wore masks. The photos of the vandalism of the entrance to the Forum's offices, the placement of sandbags and the deployment of a barbed wire fence were distributed in the media. Some of the participants They even took pride in participating in the event and willingly associated themselves with acts that constitute criminal offenses, including trespassing, trespassing, and even false imprisonment. In July, the lawyers of the Forum and N. were informed that the investigation case against all those involved was closed, and that no indictment would be filed And according to the response given to this article, it seems that there is not enough evidence for prosecution. When you compare the indictment filed against Shafi Paz and Doron Abrahami, who sprayed graffiti in Tel Aviv, the failure in handling the incident by the police and the prosecutor's office is doubly obvious. The investigation file includes 110 documents The transcripts of the interrogations of the seven detainees on the day of the incident, as well as two testimonies of those who were present at the offices at the time - one was taken at the offices, and the other at the police station. In the second testimony it is explicitly stated that the speaker is Alan Batofin, who was the head of the house at the office, while the name of the person who gave the testimony was deleted from the copy of the file, but it seems that he also gave it in Tafoin. In addition, the file contains many technical documents such as delay reports, documents Release on bail and the like, as well as the action reports of the police officers who were called to the incident. A police team was also called to the scene and collected findings and took fingerprints from signs hung on the spot and adhesive papers. Two other important documents are a message given by the CEO of the Kehalat Forum, Meir Rubin, in which he complained about his attack and identified Itai Brandes, who he says was one of the participants in the attack, as well as the transcript of Brandes' investigation. These days, hundreds of schools are still looking for who will manage them in the next school year, and thousands of schools are looking for teachers with candles. It has been talked about for years that there is a shortage of math, science and English teachers, and that in some areas there is an overall shortage of teachers. The Minister of Education himself says that there are currently about 1,700 teachers missing in the system. He just forgets that the solution already exists, he just doesn't use it.  Almost three years have passed since the last salary agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Teachers' Union, in which it was agreed that up to 6% of the teachers' position would be employed on individual contracts. And although the cogs of the public system work slowly, last summer a call was already published calling for students and graduates of advanced degrees to apply as part of a pilot for 200 jobs in the Tel Aviv and Central districts, which suffer from the most severe shortage of teachers. Within a few days, more than 700 people submitted applications, including high-tech people, graduates of the Technion and the Weizmann Institute and other universities. If they had accepted the most suitable 200 of them, they would have received a relatively high starting salary, of NIS 16-15 thousand, without tenure and with fewer bureaucratic restrictions on the managers.  How many years have we been complaining about the fact that the entry threshold for teaching does not rise? Those who applied for the individual contracts will not leave their jobs to study teaching and will not enter the narrow path of the collective agreements. They don't care that in 20 years their salary will be high, and they certainly don't care about the tenure or representation of the teachers' organizations. They want to teach, but without all the bureaucracy and dragging around.  So they published a pilot and a call for applications, but as soon as Ypa Ben David, Secretary General of the Teachers' Union, turned the table, the Ministry of Education immediately backed down and froze the pilot. Ben David's argument is ridiculous: she claims that although she signed the agreement with the individual contracts, she did not agree that the salary budget for these teachers would come at the expense of the other teachers. In other words, it is clear to everyone that they are not able to fill the required teacher positions, but Ypa Demands that the individual contracts be financed from an additional budget. This is of course an attempt to torpedo the move at the expense of the Israeli students, but the main blame lies with the Ministry of Education who insists on implementing the agreement as written and worded. Only last December, after the freeze on the individual contracts, the results of the TIMSS tests were published, and it became clear that Israel had deteriorated compared to other countries, with countries such as Malta and Cyprus following The deterioration Minister Kish announced the "establishment of an inspection team", and Kish announced a five-year plan called "Real Israel", and for the sake of its implementation, he asked for an addition of one billion shekels to the budget, and instead of putting hundreds or even thousands of excellent teachers into the system, he is repeating the mistakes of previous ministers of education and trying to take care of the educational programs and the training of the teachers Quality of teachers" - so stated a comprehensive McKinsey report almost two decades ago. After repeated failures to attract the best young people to the field of education, it seems that for the first time a possible formula has been found, but it includes a dimension of decentralization - it reduces the degree of control of the Ministry of Education over the schools and the teaching force, and it creates an alternative employment channel for the teachers' organizations. No body likes to lose power and control, but for the next school year the Ministry of Education, headed by the Minister of Education Kish, they will have to choose between the good of the students and the preservation of the centralized control and the stranglehold of the system. No excuse, not even the security situation, will absolve those who would prevent the introduction of teachers who are so lacking in the system only out of self-interested considerations. Does UNRA enjoy immunity under international law? The words of Adv. In one sentence: UNRA does not have legal immunity for 5 reasons, but especially because the organization acts contrary to its original goals and endangers the security of the citizens of Israel. ------- I want to focus on a question that will be at the center of a request for an advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice, and will also be discussed in the High Court: Does UNRA enjoy immunity under international law? The answer to this is clear - no. UNRA's immunity is not automatic, it is not understood Of course, and in fact - it does not exist in cases where the organization deviates from its goals and acts contrary to the principles of the United Nations itself. The legal background: UNRWA as a body not entitled to automatic immunity UNRWA was established by UN General Assembly Resolution 302 (IV) in December 1949. The resolution "calls" on states to grant it rights and immunities - language that indicates that this is not a binding requirement. Compare this to other decisions, such as 428 (V) which established the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, which does not contain similar wording. If immunity was not granted automatically, it is clear that it is conditional on the consent of the host countries. Indeed, in the 1950s the countries of the region were not satisfied with the UN decision. They signed separate agreements with UNRWA to regulate their status. Egypt granted immunity - but only with a formal agreement. Jordan and Lebanon did the same. That is, UNRWA's immunity depended on the will of the host countries. What is given by agreement - can also be canceled. UNRA's status in Israel - conditional consent only The basis for UNRA's activity in Israel was determined in an exchange of letters from 1967, according to which the 1946 Convention would regulate its rights and immunities. But even then, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs clarified that this is a temporary arrangement, which can be changed or canceled. The UN Secretariat itself also confirmed this in a legal opinion from 1968: "A subsidiary body of the General Assembly can operate in the territory of a country only with its consent." Simply put, Israel is entitled to stop UNRWA's activities - and this is anchored in international law. Legal rulings - UNRA's immunity is not taken for granted Courts in Jordan, Egypt and Gaza have discussed UNRA's immunity more than once. In a Jordanian case from 1954, a former employee succeeded in confiscating UNRWA funds in a bank. In 1957, an Egyptian court in Gaza ruled that UNRWA is a separate body from the UN and does not enjoy its immunity. Even if in 1970 a court in Gaza granted UNRWA immunity, the minority opinion held that it has no immunity at all. If so, UNRA's immunity is, to say the least, a controversial matter. UNRA and terrorism - is it possible to grant immunity to criminal activity? The question of immunity becomes irrelevant when considering UNRA's ties to terrorism. Already in 2004, UNRA's head at the time, Peter Hansen, admitted that "there are members of Hamas on UNRA's payroll, and I don't see that as a problem." Hamas and other terrorist organizations penetrated deeply into UNRA - weapons and tunnels were found in its schools, and UNRA officials were exposed as terrorist operatives. Section 105(1) of the UN Charter states that an organization is entitled to immunity only when it is "required to fulfill its objectives". Terrorism, terrorist financing and assistance to kidnappings are not part of the goals of the United Nations. Since 1968, 19 international treaties have been adopted to combat terrorism - none of them grant immunity to a body that cooperates with terrorist organizations. In conclusion - UNRA is not immune from the law The International Court of Justice has already determined that "international organizations are bound by the rules of international law". There is no legal rule that harbors an organization that acts contrary to the goals of the United Nations, enables terrorism, and endangers the citizens of the host country. Israel is not obligated to grant immunity to UNRA - and it is obligated to protect its sovereignty and the security of its citizens. Thank you very much.
